description: Stock outlook for a list of items (by SKU, max 100): available (net of committed, the units open sales and transfer orders hold, as the Inventory page and Shopify show it), committed, inbound, and the two days-of-supply metrics — daysOnHand (stock before committed units ÷ the planning rate, which already counts open orders: the stockout-urgency signal) and aggregatedInventoryDays (including inbound POs and buildable capacity: the procurement-planning signal) — plus velocity confidence tier, composite health score, and the sales rate with trend over the requested period (week|month|quarter). Two rates, one base: dailyConsumption is the planning rate (the higher of forecast and sales history, plus production pulls; conservative on purpose), unitsPerDay is the sales rate (what sold).

period.description: Velocity period: week, month (default), or quarter.

skus.description: Item SKUs to look up (max 100 per call).

name: get_item_stock_outlook

aggregatedInventoryDays.description: Effective inventory (including inbound POs and buildable capacity) ÷ the planning rate: the procurement-planning signal. Null means no demand signal.

available.description: Available to sell: on hand less reserved and committed units, as the Inventory page shows it.

committed.description: Units held by open sales and transfer orders, as Shopify counts committed. Already out of available.

dailyConsumption.description: Planning rate, units/day (dailyConsumption): what the warehouse plans stock for. The higher of the forecast and the sales rate (plus sales with no order behind them), raised by scheduled production and BOM pulls; at a warehouse that supplies transfer nodes it includes what they pull. Conservative on purpose. Days on hand divides by this rate.

daysOnHand.description: Stock before committed units ÷ the planning rate (dailyConsumption): the stockout-urgency signal. Committed units stay in because the planning rate already counts open orders as demand. Null means no demand signal.

unitsPerDay.description: Sales rate, units/day: net sales over the window (returns deducted, each order weighted by its forecast weight). What sold. Use it for analysis and for reorder policies written from sales.

title: Item Stock Outlook
